Take the quiz below first, read the explanation for anything you miss, then use the chapter e-book at the end for full, exam-level practice.

What CTET Paper 2 asks on Mensuration

Questions cover perimeter and area of plane figures (rectangle, square, triangle, parallelogram, circle) and the surface area and volume of cubes, cuboids and cylinders, with plenty of unit-conversion and real-life applications.

Key facts & formulas to remember

  • Perimeter of a rectangle = 2(l + b); area = l × b.
  • Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height; area of a circle = πr²; circumference = 2πr.
  • Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h; of a cube = a³; of a cylinder = πr²h.
  • Scaling a length by k multiplies area by k² and volume by k³.
  • Perimeter is in units, area in square units, volume in cubic units.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Assuming a bigger perimeter always means a bigger area.
  • Mixing up units (using cm and m in the same calculation).
  • Confusing area with perimeter, or surface area with volume.

quiz.title: CTET Mensuration Practice Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten CTET Paper II–pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: If the side of a regular hexagon is doubled, how many times does its perimeter become?
questions.explanation: The perimeter of a regular hexagon with side length s is given by P = 6s. If the side is doubled to 2s, the new perimeter is P' = 6(2s) = 2(6s) = 2P. Thus, the perimeter becomes 2 times the original.

questions.q: What is the area of a square plot of land with a side length of 120 cm in square meters?
questions.explanation: Side length s = 120 cm = 1.2 m. Area of the square = s² = (1.2 m)² = 1.44 m².

questions.q: A rectangular floor has a length of 8 m and a breadth of 5 m. Find the cost of carpeting the floor at the rate of ₹150 per m².
questions.explanation: Area of the floor = length × breadth = 8 m × 5 m = 40 m². Total cost = Area × Rate = 40 × 150 = ₹6,000.

questions.q: If the circumference of a circular wheel is 220 cm, what is its radius? (Use π = 22/7)
questions.explanation: Circumference C = 2π r. Given 220 = 2 × 22/7 × r. Therefore, r = (220 × 7)/(2 × 22) = 1540/44 = 35 cm.

questions.q: What is the total surface area of a wooden cube whose edge is 6 cm?
questions.explanation: Total surface area of a cube = 6a², where a is the edge length. Here, a = 6 cm. Total surface area = 6 × (6)² = 6 × 36 = 216 cm².

questions.q: Find the volume of a cubic container whose edge length is 0.5 m.
questions.explanation: Volume of a cube = a³. Here, a = 0.5 m. Volume = (0.5)³ = 0.125 m³.

questions.q: The base of a triangular field is three times its height. If the cost of cultivating the field at ₹25 per 100 m² is ₹600, find the height of the triangle.
questions.explanation: Total cost = Area × (Rate/100), so Area × (25/100) = 600, giving Area = (600 × 100)/25 = 2400 m². Let the height be h; then the base b = 3h. Area of a triangle = (1/2) × b × h = (1/2) × 3h × h = 1.5h². Setting 1.5h² = 2400 gives h² = 1600, so h = 40 m.

questions.q: The inner circumference of a circular track is 352 m. If the track is uniformly 7 m wide everywhere, find the area of the track. (Use π = 22/7)
A metallic cuboid measuring 12 cm × 9 cm × 2 cm is melted and recast into a solid cube. What is the total surface area of the cube so formed?
questions.explanation: Volume of the cuboid = 12 × 9 × 2 = 216 cm³. Since the metal is simply recast, the cube has the same volume, so edge³ = 216, giving edge = ∛216 = 6 cm. Total surface area of the cube = 6 × edge² = 6 × 36 = 216 cm².

questions.q: A cuboidal room is 10 m long, 5 m wide, and 3 m high. Find the cost of whitewashing its four walls and ceiling at the rate of ₹25 per m².
questions.explanation: Area to be whitewashed = area of four walls + area of ceiling = 2h(l+b) + (l×b) = 2(3)(10+5) + (10×5) = 90 + 50 = 140 m². Total cost = 140 × 25 = ₹3,500.

faq.q: Do two shapes with the same perimeter have the same area?
faq.a: No. Figures with equal perimeters can have very different areas — a square gives the maximum area for a given perimeter.

faq.q: What value of π should I use?
faq.a: Use 22/7 or 3.14 as directed in the question; 22/7 is convenient when the radius is a multiple of 7.
